questions.q: Which of the following is the correct Itô multiplication rule?
options: (dW_t)² = 0
(dW_t)² = dt
(dt)² = dt
dt · dW_t = dt
questions.explain: Because Brownian motion's quadratic variation over [0,t] equals t, the informal rule is (dW_t)² = dt — this nonzero term is what distinguishes stochastic calculus from ordinary calculus.

questions.q: For dX_t = μdt + σdW_t and a twice-differentiable f(t,x), what does Itô's lemma state for df?
options: df = f_x dX_t only, exactly like the ordinary chain rule
df = [f_t + μf_x + ½σ²f_xx] dt + σf_x dW_t
df = [f_t + μf_x] dt only, with no second-derivative term
df = σ²f_xx dt, with no first-derivative term at all
questions.explain: Itô's lemma adds the correction term ½σ²f_xx (from the nonzero quadratic variation) to what the ordinary chain rule would give, alongside the usual f_t and μf_x drift terms and the σf_x dW diffusion term.

questions.q: Applying Itô's lemma to f(S) = ln(S) under dS_t = μS_t dt + σS_t dW_t gives which SDE for d(ln S_t)?
options: d(ln S_t) = μ dt + σ dW_t
d(ln S_t) = (μ − ½σ²) dt + σ dW_t
d(ln S_t) = (μ + ½σ²) dt + σ dW_t
d(ln S_t) = σ² dt
questions.explain: With f_S = 1/S and f_SS = −1/S², Itô's lemma gives d(ln S) = [μS·(1/S) + ½σ²S²·(−1/S²)]dt + σS·(1/S)dW = (μ − ½σ²)dt + σdW.

questions.q: What is the exact closed-form solution to dS_t = μS_t dt + σS_t dW_t (geometric Brownian motion)?
options: S_t = S_0 + μt + σW_t
S_t = S_0 exp[(μ − ½σ²)t + σW_t]
S_t = S_0 exp[μt + σW_t]
S_t = S_0 exp[σ²t]
questions.explain: Integrating d(ln S_t) = (μ−½σ²)dt + σdW_t from 0 to t (with W_0=0) gives ln(S_t) − ln(S_0) = (μ−½σ²)t + σW_t, i.e. S_t = S_0 exp[(μ−½σ²)t + σW_t].

questions.q: Why does the empirical mean of ln(S_T/S_0) in a GBM simulation match (μ − ½σ²)T rather than μT?
options: Because the simulation code contains a bug
Because Itô's lemma adds a genuine −½σ² drift correction when converting from the price process to the log-price process, which a naive dS/S = μdt + σdW substitution would miss
Because Brownian motion has nonzero mean
Because μ and σ are always equal in practice
questions.explain: The −½σ² term is a real mathematical consequence of Itô's lemma (from the nonzero quadratic variation of Brownian motion), not a simulation artifact — it is exactly why log-price drift differs from the raw proportional drift μ.
